provenance.builtDuring: Phase 3.8.2 (Real Windows Replay & Presentation Reliability) - rebuilt to package: (1) a combined Start-Service-&-Replay action so Service Replay never hits an avoidable 'start a service first' dead-end, (2) a guard on the Run Full Service quick scenario so it can no longer hit an avoidable 'service already active' error, and (3) two presentation-display reliability fixes - initial-state hydration on mount and synchronous close reconciliation - addressing the operator's reported 'CIP Presentation Display (Not Responding)' and reopen-failure symptoms
provenance.buildEnvironment: cross-compiled from Linux using rustup target x86_64-pc-windows-gnu, gcc-mingw-w64, and nsis (makensis) - identical toolchain to every prior phase, see docs/phase-3-4-windows-pilot.md for the original toolchain setup and docs/phase-3-8-2-service-replay-reliability.md for what changed this phase
provenance.note: This artifact supersedes the Phase 3.8.1 installer (previously SHA-256 a5c17483876a1ddfa2d3c2e1b5a6a7ef4c1c73e86e0949b146dd91f0c0f3cf2f) because this phase modified apps/desktop/src-tauri/src/commands.rs (PresentationDisplayState gains activeSlide; close_presentation_display now synchronously reconciles), apps/desktop/src-tauri/src/presentation.rs (test only), apps/desktop/src/components/servicereplay/ServiceReplay.tsx (combined start-and-replay action, guarded Run Full Service), apps/desktop/src/components/PresentationDisplay.tsx (mount-time state hydration), and added apps/desktop/src/components/presentationDisplayHydration.ts. Zero new Tauri commands, zero new migrations, zero intelligence engine changes - see docs/phase-3-8-2-audit.md for the full architectural-safety diff. This is a freshly compiled build (`cargo build --release --target x86_64-pc-windows-gnu` via `tauri build`), not a copy of a prior artifact.

releaseCandidateStatement: This is the Phase 3.8.2 SOFTWARE RELEASE CANDIDATE for Windows x64 (Real Windows Replay & Presentation Reliability). It is a real, verifiable build artifact - not a placeholder, not a simulation, not a fabrication. See docs/phase-3-8-2-service-replay-reliability.md for the full PASS/HOLD breakdown and final gate.
physicalHardwareStatement: Physical hardware qualification has NOT been performed in the build environment. This installer has not been installed, launched, or tested on any real Windows machine. No real microphone, no real Whisper transcription, no real second display/projector, and no real human operator workflow has been exercised against this build. Xvfb, simulated audio, virtual displays, automated tests, Service Replay, and cross-compilation success are Environment A/B evidence only and are never substituted for Environment C (real hardware) evidence anywhere in this project's documentation. The operator's own Phase 3.8.1 Windows testing (which reported the defects this phase fixes - Evidence A-D) is real Environment C usage of the PRIOR (Phase 3.8.1) build, not of this rebuilt artifact - per this phase's own explicit instruction, that prior test is never converted into PASS evidence for this rebuild. The operator's own stated hard blocker for this phase (the same Windows laptop successfully completing a full replay-to-presentation-reopen cycle on THIS rebuilt artifact) has not been met.
githubReleaseStatus: NOT CONFIGURED - no .github/workflows directory exists in this repository, and no GitHub Release has been created for this artifact. This installer is available only via this repository's working tree (release/windows/), not via GitHub Releases or any CI/CD pipeline.
obtainingWithoutDeveloperTooling: The file at release/windows/Church Intelligence Platform_0.1.0_x64-setup.exe can be copied/transferred directly (e.g. via a git clone of this repository, a direct file download, or a USB drive) to the target Windows machine and run there. Running the installer on Windows requires none of: Claude Code, Rust, Cargo, Node.js, npm, or the CIP source tree - only the .exe file itself.
knownLimitations: UNSIGNED release candidate - Windows SmartScreen will show an 'unknown publisher' warning on first run
Cross-compiled from Linux, never launch-tested on real Windows hardware - Environment C remains not performed for THIS rebuilt artifact

The exact mechanism behind the operator's reported literal 'Not Responding' Windows title-bar text was not, and could not be, proven in this environment (no WinDbg/ETW/physical Windows access) - two real, independently provable races were identified and fixed by code trace alone, but this session does not claim to have confirmed which failure mode the operator observed

Music Library is legitimately empty in a production build - no licensed production song dataset exists in this repository; Service Replay's default flow does not exercise Music Intelligence for this reason

The ground-up visual/UX redesign described aspirationally in the original Phase 3.8 spec was deliberately not attempted this phase either - scope remained limited to the specific reliability defects the operator reported
See docs/phase-3-8-2-service-replay-reliability.md and pilot-evidence/3.8.2/ for the full Environment A/B/C evidence breakdown
